subject: chemistry
title: Redox Processes Adventure 3: Standard potentials, EMF and electrolysis quantities
welcome_lead: Today you'll calculate EMF from standard potentials — and quantify electrolysis with Faraday.
meta_desc: Chemistry HL — standard electrode potentials, EMF, Nernst, Faraday's laws, electroplating.
final_note: You learned E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode; positive E° → spontaneous; charge Q = It; mass deposited via n = Q/(zF).

concepts.def: E° cell; if positive, reaction spontaneous

walkthroughs.body_html:
E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode (both as reduction).

Zn|Zn²⁺ ||Cu²⁺|Cu: E° = 0.34 − (−0.76) = +1.10 V. Positive → spontaneous.

Use most positive E° as cathode (reduction); other becomes anode (oxidation).

Q = I × t (coulombs = amps × seconds).

Moles of electrons = Q / F, where F = 96,500 C/mol.

For Mⁿ⁺ + n e⁻ → M: moles M = moles e⁻ / n.

Example: 0.5 A for 1 hour through Cu²⁺.
Q = 0.5 × 3600 = 1800 C.
n(e⁻) = 1800/96500 = 0.01865 mol.
n(Cu) = 0.01865/2 = 0.00933 mol = 0.593 g Cu.

Electroplating uses electrolysis to coat objects:

- Chrome (Cr) on car parts — corrosion resistance.
- Silver (Ag) on cutlery.
- Gold (Au) on connectors.

Object = cathode; pure metal = anode; salt solution = electrolyte.

International perspective: aluminium production (Hall-Héroult process, 1886) electrolyses Al₂O₃ in cryolite — uses ~3-5% of world electricity globally.

mcqs.q: EMF of a cell is calculated by:
Can a single standard electrode potential be measured in isolation?
options: No — electrode potentials are RELATIVE values measured against a reference (the standard hydrogen electrode, defined as 0 V).
Each electrode has an absolute potential that can be measured directly with a voltmeter.
Standard electrode potentials are measured by submerging the electrode in pure water.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.

mcqs.q: If E°cell for a redox reaction is positive, what does that tell you?
options: A positive E°cell guarantees the reaction will happen rapidly at room temperature.
The reaction is thermodynamically feasible — but it may still be very slow if kinetic barriers are high.
A positive E°cell means the reaction is exothermic in every case.
Standard electrode potentials are measured by submerging the electrode in pure water.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
A positive E°cell means the reaction is exothermic in every case.
Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.
Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.
